_about: Verification pass, 4 Nov 2026. Documents read in the DOJ release text (EFTA numbers link to justice.gov) and checked against news reports. Status upgrades, new documented ties, ; five private individuals with no documented role were removed from the published map.

nodes.name: Plan D, LLC
nodes.note: US Virgin Islands company; Epstein signed as its sole member. Listed as the holder of the Gulfstream G550 N212JE, and the borrower of $30.5M from Leon Black's BV70 LLC in 2017.

nodes.name: BV70 LLC
nodes.note: New York company owned by Leon Black, addressed care of Elysium Management. Lent Epstein's Plan D $30.5M in 2017 (Dechert review for Apollo, 2021); reported as the route for Black's $10M to Gratitude America.

nodes.name: Gulfstream G550 N212JE
nodes.note: Aircraft listed against Plan D, LLC in Epstein's own aircraft list in the release.

nodes.name: Boeing 727 N908JE
nodes.note: Owned by JEGE, Inc., per a 2006 FBI interview with one of Epstein's pilots; seats up to 26.

nodes.name: Gulfstream N909JE
nodes.note: Owned and operated by Hyperion Air, Inc., per the same 2006 FBI interview; seats up to 12. The pilot said Epstein kept a separate company for each plane for liability reasons.

nodes.name: Stacey Plaskett
nodes.note: Delegate to Congress for the US Virgin Islands. Texted with Epstein during a February 2019 House hearing; a House censure resolution over it failed in November 2025. Received campaign donations from Epstein's accountants (reported). Not accused of a crime.

nodes.name: William Barr
nodes.note: US Attorney General 2019–2020; in August 2019 said there were 'serious irregularities' at the jail where Epstein died. Son of Donald Barr, the Dalton headmaster. Nothing in the record ties him to the Dalton hire; the family tie is shown only so the two are not confused.

nodes.name: White House tour, 27 Dec 2015
nodes.note: Woody Allen, Soon-Yi Previn and Kathryn Ruemmler visited on 27 Dec 2015 after Epstein asked Ruemmler in May 2015 to show them the White House (NBC, from released emails and White House visitor records).

nodes.name: Stanley Pottinger
nodes.note: Lawyer for Epstein survivors. In May 2016 he forwarded to an SDNY prosecutor Jean-Luc Brunel's description of Daniel Siad as a scout or recruiter for Epstein (email in the release).

nodes.name: Euro payment instruction to Daniel Siad, 30 Apr 2014
nodes.note: Attachment named 'DB JEE Custody Account_Daniel Siad Euros_4-30-2014' sent by Richard Kahn to Deutsche Bank on 25 Apr 2014, copied to Darren Indyke and Bella Klein. The release shows the instruction; the attachment's amount and the transfer's completion are not in the copy read.

nodes.name: Court motion on Epstein's investigators, 2009
nodes.note: S.D. Fla. case 9:08-cv-80119, docket 299 (15 Sep 2009): records that Epstein 'employed private investigators to contact third-parties believed familiar with' plaintiffs to gather background on them; plaintiffs sought to stop the contacts.

nodes.name: Function: command and inner circle
nodes.note: How a network concentrates decisions in a few trusted people. Compared: Sinaloa (Guzmán's controlled phones), NXIVM (first-line 'masters'). Epstein record: Maxwell; four assistants named in the 2008 deal; office staff.

nodes.name: Function: recruitment through legitimate fronts
nodes.note: Compared: NXIVM's 'mentorship group' pretext; Nygård's company, modelling promises and staff screening. Epstein record: funding of MC2 Model Management; a scout paid from his account; 'massage' work.

nodes.name: Function: payroll and money through companies
nodes.note: Compared: Nygård Group funds and payroll ('models', 'assistants'); cartel money handling. Epstein record: HBRK Associates, Southern Trust, LSJE payroll, Plan D, Kahn's payment instructions.

nodes.name: Function: logistics and transport
nodes.note: Compared: Sinaloa tunnels and aircraft. Epstein record: a separate company for each plane (JEGE, Hyperion, Plan D); private island; residences.

nodes.name: Function: influence over officials
nodes.note: Compared: García Luna, convicted in 2023 of taking Sinaloa bribes. Epstein record: no bribe documented; political donations, tax breaks, texts with a delegate, and the 2008 deal are on file.

nodes.name: Function: silencing accusers and reporters
nodes.note: Compared: Weinstein's hired intelligence firms (Black Cube, Kroll); Nygård's alleged paid false affidavits and threats. Epstein record: investigators contacting plaintiffs' acquaintances (2009 court motion); reported surveillance of victims' families.

nodes.name: Function: institutions that were told and did not act
nodes.note: Compared: FBI and Nassar (2021 inspector general), BBC and Savile (2016 review), Pennsylvania dioceses (2018 grand jury). Epstein record: FBI complaint 1996; banks' internal warnings; a 2016 tip to SDNY.

nodes.name: Function: records and the insider who opens them
nodes.note: Compared: Guzmán's IT technician who gave the FBI access to his encrypted phones. Epstein record: no insider cooperated publicly; the case rests on emails, bank records and survivors.

nodes.name: Comparison case: Sinaloa cartel (Guzmán trial 2019; García Luna 2023)
nodes.note: Drug network. Documented at trial: encrypted phone system built by an IT technician who became an FBI informant; bribes to police and officials; cross-border tunnels. Mexico's former security chief convicted in New York in Feb 2023 of taking cartel bribes; sentenced to 38+ years.

nodes.name: Comparison case: NXIVM (Raniere, convicted 2019)
nodes.note: Convicted June 2019 of racketeering and sex trafficking; 120 years. Recruited women under the pretext of a women-only mentorship group; demanded 'collateral' to stop members leaving or talking.

nodes.name: Comparison case: Nygård (charged 2020; convicted in Canada)
nodes.note: US indictment (SDNY, Dec 2020; allegations): used his company's employees, funds and payroll to recruit and keep victims; 'pamper parties'; paid for false statements and threatened witnesses. Convicted in Toronto of four sexual assaults; sentenced to 11 years.

nodes.name: Comparison case: Weinstein's investigators
nodes.note: New Yorker reporting (2017): hired Kroll and Black Cube to gather information on accusers and journalists; one contract's stated aim was to stop publication.

nodes.name: Comparison case: FBI and Nassar (inspector general, 2021)
nodes.note: FBI Indianapolis told in 2015; little action for months; at least 40 more girls and women reported abuse over 14 months while the FBI knew; officials gave inaccurate information to internal inquiries.

nodes.name: Comparison case: BBC and Savile (Smith review, 2016)
nodes.note: 72 victims; complaints disbelieved or covered up; a junior worker told 'he is a VIP'; the BBC more concerned with reputation.

nodes.name: Comparison case: Pennsylvania dioceses (grand jury, 2018)
nodes.note: 300+ priests, 1,000+ children identified; euphemisms, untrained internal investigators, reassignment, police discouraged: a 'playbook for concealing the truth'.

nodes.name: Comparison case: Combs verdict (2025)
nodes.note: Jury acquitted Sean Combs of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking in July 2025 and convicted on Mann Act transportation counts. A reminder that an 'enterprise' has to be proven, not inferred from wealth and staff.

node_notes.bella_klein: Assistant Controller at HBRK Associates, Richard Kahn's accounting firm, and an accountant there since November 1999, per a 2019 TD Bank suspicious-activity report in the release (a bank report, not a finding). Listed as a contact for HBRK's accounts. Not accused of a crime. Email counts come from a secondary research export and are not checked.
node_notes.hbrk: HBRK Associates Inc., 575 Lexington Avenue, New York: Richard Kahn's accounting firm. Wires from Epstein, Southern Trust, Southern Financial and Darren K. Indyke PLLC accounts were addressed 'c/o HBRK Associates' (TD Bank SAR, 2019). It described itself to the bank as serving ultra-high-net-worth clients other than Epstein.
node_notes.firstbank: FirstBank Puerto Rico / FirstBank VI. A 6 Apr 2016 internal memo calls Epstein a 'large non-borrowing deposit Platinum Banking client' with several companies' accounts, an average combined balance over $5.3M, banking there for over seven years; it waived his service and wire fees. A grand-jury subpoena went to the bank on 31 Dec 2019. Earlier reporting (WSJ) called him a 'legacy relationship' from its 2002 purchase of Chase's USVI operations.
node_notes.network_functions: Search framework built from documented cases (Sinaloa, NXIVM, Nygård, Weinstein, the FBI and Nassar, the BBC and Savile, Pennsylvania dioceses, the Combs verdict). Each function becomes a question asked of the Epstein files. Comparison nodes are not ties to Epstein; only Epstein-specific documents count as evidence.
